PSI-10.name: ACME Flame Design
PSI-10.blurb: Gaseous ethylene flames in the ACME hardware, used to study normal and inverse flame structure rather than a spacecraft material.

relevance.iss: Maps how a gaseous flame sits in the CIR, which is context for material tests but not a flammability limit for cabin fabrics.
relevance.moon: Inverse flames change where the oxygen is, a useful bound when habitat oxygen is enriched, but the fuel is ethylene gas.
relevance.suit: Not a spacesuit-atmosphere materials test. Oxygen in these runs is a flame-structure variable.
relevance.earth: Fundamental gaseous-flame structure, weak link to terrestrial firefighting gear.

PSI-20.name: ACME Burning Rate Emulator
PSI-20.blurb: Burning Rate Emulator studied material flammability in a still atmosphere by matching the burning rate of a solid with a gaseous burner.

relevance.iss: Still-atmosphere flammability is the no-ventilation limit inside a rack or a closed volume on station.
relevance.moon: Oxygen was varied from about 21 percent up through the mid-30s and 40 percent, the range expected in a lunar habitat.
relevance.suit: The high-oxygen BRE points are the closest still-air screen to a suit atmosphere short of the CFI-G burner.
relevance.earth: A method for screening materials without a large fire, not a detector or turnout-gear result.

PSI-21.name: ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
PSI-21.blurb: Coflow laminar diffusion flames of gaseous fuel in ACME. Supporting combustion science, not a solid-material flammability test.

relevance.iss: Shows how a laminar jet flame behaves without buoyancy. Indirect for cabin material selection.
relevance.moon: Coflow speed is a stand-in for ventilation, but the fuel is gas, not habitat plastic or fabric.
relevance.suit: Does not address 100 percent oxygen at suit pressure.
relevance.earth: Laboratory flame structure, not firefighter equipment.

PSI-22.name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
PSI-22.blurb: Electric-field effects on laminar diffusion flames. PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data yet; this experiment used the electric field on flame ions to mimic a body force.

relevance.iss: A gaseous-flame body-force study. Secondary to BASS and SAME for station operations.
relevance.moon: The Moon is partial gravity. Until LUCI and FM2 fly, E-FIELD is the PSI stand-in that puts a force on the flame.
relevance.suit: Does not reproduce suit oxygen concentration.
relevance.earth: Ion-driven flow is a research tool, not a fire-service product.

PSI-23.name: ACME s-Flame
PSI-23.blurb: Structure and response of spherical diffusion flames in ACME. The microgravity flame shape (a sphere fed by diffusion) is the basic picture behind freefall fire.

relevance.iss: Explains why a station flame is spherical and diffusion-limited once buoyancy is gone.
relevance.moon: Spherical flames are the zero-g end of the bound. Lunar gravity sits between this and a normal flame.
relevance.suit: Shape study, not a suit-material limit.
relevance.earth: The contrast with a teardrop flame is teaching material, not a product.

PSI-25.name: BASS-II
PSI-25.blurb: Burning and Suppression of Solids II. Solid fuels in a ventilated duct on the ISS, with oxygen recorded on the test matrix.

relevance.iss: Directly the materials and the low-speed ventilation a crew cabin actually has.
relevance.moon: Solid fuels (films, fabrics) plus a measured oxygen level are what a lunar habitat material screen needs.
relevance.suit: Shows how the same solids behave as oxygen rises, which is the direction a suit prebreathe and cabin move.
relevance.earth: Suppression and spread on thin materials informs how fabrics burn, loosely related to turnout gear.

PSI-26.name: BASS
PSI-26.blurb: Burning and Suppression of Solids. Bridged the NASA-STD-6001 ground test and real microgravity flammability, and tried a gaseous extinguisher like the ISS agent.

relevance.iss: SIBAL fabric and PMMA in the glovebox duct, plus a nitrogen-style extinguisher already used on station.
relevance.moon: Thicker, realistic solids in a forced flow. Habitat oxygen will be higher than these early runs, so read them as the low-oxygen bound.
relevance.suit: Useful geometry (fire behind an object, wake flames) but not 100 percent oxygen.
relevance.earth: Extinguisher effectiveness on small solids. The flight hardware is not a ground extinguisher.

PSI-39.name: Cool Flames Investigation
PSI-39.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus in the CIR
PSI-39.blurb: Cool flames around liquid-fuel droplets. A flame can look out and still be burning in a cool-flame mode, which matters for declaring a fire extinguished.

relevance.iss: Droplet fuels in cabin atmospheres. Cool-flame survival means a visible extinction is not always the end of combustion.
relevance.moon: Oxygen and diluent were varied. Cool flames are a suppression false-negative, not a materials limit.
relevance.earth: Explains reignition after an apparent extinguishment. Indirect for terrestrial nozzles.

PSI-47.name: DAFT / DAFT-2
PSI-47.blurb: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test. The smoke instrument from SAME was pointed at dust instead of smoke.

relevance.iss: Nuisance dust on station is why a smoke detector false-alarms. DAFT measures that background.
relevance.moon: Lunar dust is the same problem, sharper. A detector that cannot tell dust from smoke will alarm whenever the habitat is dirty.
relevance.earth: This is the flight root of the shuttle detector that separates smoke from dust, later used in mines.

PSI-60.name: SPICE data analysis
PSI-60.blurb: Computational analysis of the Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment. A paper-scale study, not a new flight test.

relevance.iss: Soot-point models support how much smoke a detector might see. Secondary to SAME itself.
relevance.moon: No habitat oxygen or dust measurement.
relevance.earth: Soot modeling only.

PSI-62.name: Concurrent flame spread vs BASS
PSI-62.blurb: Concurrent flame-spread modeling with flamelet-generated manifolds, checked against BASS. A model, not a new burn.

relevance.iss: A way to extrapolate BASS spread instead of burning every material on station.
relevance.moon: The model is only as good as the BASS oxygen range it was checked against.
relevance.earth: Numerical method, not hardware.

PSI-68.name: FLEX-2
PSI-68.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus in the CIR
PSI-68.blurb: Second Flame Extinguishment Experiment. Liquid droplets in oxygen-nitrogen or oxygen-helium, with a small imposed flow.

relevance.iss: Extinction of droplet flames when oxygen, pressure, and a slow flow change. That is the suppression corner of station fire safety.
relevance.moon: Oxygen mole fractions in the test matrix reach about 0.30, which touches the lunar-habitat band.
relevance.earth: Helium and nitrogen dilution is the same idea as inerting a compartment.

PSI-69.name: FLEX
PSI-69.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus in the CIR
PSI-69.blurb: Flame Extinguishment Experiment. Droplets of liquid fuel in atmospheres diluted with carbon dioxide or helium, the two suppressants studied for spacecraft.

relevance.iss: The suppression dataset: carbon dioxide and helium dilution, with oxygen mole fraction and droplet size for hundreds of burns.
relevance.moon: Most runs sit near Earth oxygen. Use it for the suppressant, not for a 30 percent oxygen material limit.
relevance.suit: Does not cover a pure-oxygen suit.
relevance.earth: Fine water mist for the ISS came from this suppression line of work and is used on the ground. Dilution limits travel the same way.

PSI-98.name: Saffire-I
PSI-98.hardware: Cygnus vehicle after departure from the ISS
PSI-98.blurb: First large-scale spacecraft fire. A cotton-fiberglass blend about a meter long, burned in Cygnus after it left the station.

relevance.iss: The first burn bigger than an index card in a real spacecraft volume, at cabin oxygen near 21 percent and a set airflow.
relevance.moon: Scale is right for a habitat. Oxygen in Saffire-I is still the station value, so it is the low-oxygen large-fire bound.
relevance.suit: Too big and too lean to be a suit fire. It bounds the vehicle the suit returns to.
relevance.earth: Large-sample spread in a confined volume is a research result, not a ground product.

PSI-99.name: Saffire-II
PSI-99.hardware: Cygnus vehicle after departure from the ISS
PSI-99.blurb: Nine materials on one card, including silicone, Nomex, and the acrylic used for spacecraft windows, burned at spacecraft scale.

relevance.iss: The material menu for a cabin: silicone, Nomex, PMMA, SIBAL, at about 20 cm/s and about 21 percent oxygen.
relevance.moon: Same solids a habitat will fly. Oxygen is still near 21 percent, so treat spread rates as a lower bound.
relevance.suit: Nomex and silicone are suit-adjacent materials, but the test atmosphere is not 100 percent oxygen at 4.3 psi.
relevance.earth: Nomex and silicone results are the closest flight data to protective clothing.

PSI-100.name: Saffire-III
PSI-100.hardware: Cygnus vehicle after departure from the ISS
PSI-100.blurb: Same cotton-fiberglass blend as Saffire-I, burned at a higher flow so ventilation can be compared at spacecraft scale.

relevance.iss: Raises the airflow on a meter-scale sample. Ventilation is what feeds a station fire once buoyancy is gone.
relevance.moon: Flow comparison at large scale. Oxygen is still the station mix.
relevance.earth: Confined-flow spread, indirect.

PSI-101.name: SAME-R
PSI-101.blurb: Reflight of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment after the first unit's samples were contaminated. Sizes the liquid smoke droplets that form in low gravity.

relevance.iss: The detector design input: droplet size and how fast smoke moves when there is no buoyant plume.
relevance.moon: Particle sizes still apply. Dust interference is DAFT, not SAME-R.
relevance.earth: Low-gravity particle sizes explain why a spacecraft detector is built differently from a ceiling alarm.

PSI-102.name: SAME
PSI-102.blurb: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment. Overheated Teflon, Kapton, silicone, lampwick, and wire, with airflow and weight-loss rate recorded.

relevance.iss: Primary detection dataset. Smoke in microgravity does not rise, so particle size and the forced flow set the alarm.
relevance.moon: The materials are spacecraft materials. Pair it with DAFT before trusting an alarm in dust.
relevance.suit: Does not size smoke inside a suit.
relevance.earth: The shuttle detector that ignores dust grew out of this smoke-versus-nuisance work, including mining use.

PSI-106.name: SLICE
PSI-106.blurb: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment. Gaseous flames in the same duct family as BASS and SPICE.

relevance.iss: Liftoff and flame structure in the glovebox duct. Background for BASS, not the material limit.
relevance.moon: No enriched-oxygen solid sample.
relevance.earth: Not a product path.

PSI-107.name: SPICE
PSI-107.blurb: Smoke Point In Co-flow. The flow duct later shared with BASS and SLICE. Measures when a flame starts making soot.

relevance.iss: Soot onset changes what a smoke detector sees. Secondary to SAME's particle sizes.
relevance.moon: No lunar-oxygen materials matrix.
relevance.earth: Smoke-point data is a combustion metric, weakly tied to alarms.

PSI-108.name: STDCE-1
PSI-108.blurb: Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment. Liquid free-surface flow driven by temperature, not a fire-safety burn.

relevance.iss: Included because it is combustion-adjacent fluid physics in the archive. It does not set a flammability limit.
relevance.moon: No oxygen or material flammability result.
relevance.earth: No fire-service result.

PSI-115.name: SAME smoke modeling
PSI-115.blurb: Uses SAME measurements to model smoke generation in microgravity. The report is the NNX17AF08A final report.

relevance.iss: Turns SAME particle data into a smoke field a detector designer can place a sensor in.
relevance.moon: The model inherits SAME's materials and flows, not a lunar dust case.
relevance.earth: Smoke-transport modeling is how a less-nuisance detector gets its thresholds.

PSI-117.name: Cool-flame perturbation
PSI-117.blurb: External thermo-convective perturbation of cool flames, from the Farouk papers and a dissertation. Extinction diameters and oscillation, not a cabin test.

relevance.iss: Cool-flame extinction diameter is a suppression limit for small droplets after FLEX.
relevance.moon: Pressure and fuel studies. Not a habitat material.
relevance.earth: Extinction-diameter correlations are research results.

PSI-142.name: Cool-flame counterflow
PSI-142.blurb: Quantitative studies of cool-flame transitions at radiation and stretch extinction in counterflow. A data index more than a flight matrix.

relevance.iss: Stretch and radiation extinction bound when a cool flame dies. Secondary to FLEX.
relevance.moon: No habitat oxygen series in the table we hold.
relevance.earth: Counterflow extinction is a lab method.

PSI-159.name: ACME CFI-G
PSI-159.blurb: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. An oxygen-nitrogen mixture, up to about 85 percent oxygen, flows from the spherical burner into a fuel-nitrogen chamber. The highest-oxygen microgravity tests in this set.

relevance.iss: Most station air is 21 percent oxygen. CFI-G is the enriched-oxygen extreme, not the daily cabin.
relevance.moon: A lunar habitat is expected at 30 percent oxygen or more, at 10.2 psi or less. CFI-G is the only PSI series that reaches well above that, up to about 85 percent.
relevance.suit: A suit is 100 percent oxygen at 4.3 psi. CFI-G does not hit 4.3 psi, but it is the high-oxygen flame data that bounds suit fire behavior.
relevance.earth: High-oxygen burner flames are not a ground fire-service dataset.
